title: Roundcube Patches 12 Webmail Flaws Including Zero-Click Stored XSS and SSRF Bypass
content_md: Roundcube has released versions 1.6.19 and 1.7.4 to address 12 security vulnerabilities in its webmail platform, including a zero-click stored cross-site scripting flaw and a server-side request forgery bypass in its CSS proxy component. The updates, published on September 6, 2026, affect supported Roundcube 1.6.x long-term support deployments and 1.7.x installations. The project urged administrators to update production systems promptly, as several fixes address weaknesses that could let attackers bypass content restrictions, inject malicious HTML or CSS, manipulate mail headers, or access unintended internal resources. Roundcube Patches 12 Webmail Flaws The most significant issue is a zero-click stored XSS vulnerability involving the injection of TNEF MIME tags into attachment URLs. TNEF, or Transport Neutral Encapsulation Format, is a Microsoft email attachment format commonly associated with “winmail.dat” files. A malicious email could potentially embed crafted MIME metadata that causes attacker-controlled script content to be stored and executed when a recipient accesses the affected message or attachment interface. Because exploitation may not require a victim to click a malicious link, the flaw increases the risk of account compromise, session theft, or unauthorized actions in webmail.
